paragraphs: Tactile Systems Technology, Inc. ("we," "us," and "our") is a medical technology company that develops and provides innovative medical devices for the treatment of underserved chronic diseases. We were originally incorporated in Minnesota under the name Tactile Systems Technology, Inc. on January 30, 1995. During 2006, we established a merger corporation and subsequently, on July 21, 2006, merged with and into this merger corporation resulting in us being reincorporated as a Delaware corporation. The resulting corporation assumed the name Tactile Systems Technology, Inc. and in September 2013, we began doing business as "Tactile Medical".

Our mission is to help people suffering from chronic diseases live better and care for themselves at home. We focus our efforts on advancing the standard of care in treating underserved chronic diseases in the home to improve patient outcomes and quality of life and help control rising healthcare expenditures. Our areas of therapeutic focus are (1) vascular disease, with a goal of advancing the standard of care in treating lymphedema and chronic venous insufficiency, (2) oncology, where lymphedema is a common consequence among cancer survivors and (3) providing airway clearance therapy for those suffering from chronic respiratory conditions. We possess a unique, scalable platform to deliver at-home healthcare solutions throughout the United States. This evolving home care delivery model is recognized by policymakers and insurance payers as a key for controlling rising healthcare costs. Our solutions deliver cost-effective, clinically proven, long-term treatment for people with these chronic diseases.

We generally employ a direct-to-patient and -provider model within our lymphedema portfolio, through which we obtain patient referrals from clinicians, manage insurance claims on behalf of our patients and their clinicians, deliver our solutions directly to patients and train them on the proper use of our solutions. This model allows us to engage directly with patients and clinicians, which are both critical audiences to which we can provide clinical evidence and education. For our respiratory therapy product, we have a durable medical equipment ("DME") distribution model, through which we sell the AffloVest product to accredited DME providers, whose representatives gather and submit documentation for payer reimbursement, train patients on use of the device, and provide ongoing patient support.

For the year ended December 31, 2025, we generated revenue of $329.5 million and had net income of $19.1 million. Our revenue increased 12% during the year ended December 31, 2025, compared to the year ended December 31, 2024.

Lymphedema is a type of chronic swelling, or edema, which occurs in the arms, legs, neck, trunk, chest or other body parts when the lymphatic vessels are unable to adequately drain protein-rich lymph fluid from these regions. Lymphedema is progressive in nature, worsens over time, and has no known cure. Chronic venous insufficiency is a condition that occurs when the venous wall and/or valves in the veins are not working effectively, making it difficult for blood to return to the heart from the affected region(s). Phlebolymphedema is the convergence of lymphedema and chronic venous insufficiency. When the venous system does not effectively transfer blood from the lower limbs, it can result in venous hypertension and the development of painful, slow-healing wounds on the lower leg called venous leg ulcers. Venous hypertension can also lead to a marked increase in fluid build-up in the limbs, overwhelming the lymphatic system and causing lymphedema. Our proprietary Flexitouch, Entre and Nimbl systems are clinically proven at-home solutions for patients with vascular disorders such as lymphedema. Patients with lymphedema are typically treated by vascular surgeons, vascular medicine physicians, oncology care teams, wound physicians, nurses and therapists.

Our current lymphedema products are the Flexitouch Plus, Entre Plus and Nimbl systems. A predecessor to our Flexitouch system received 510(k) clearance from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (the "FDA") in July 2002, and we introduced the system to address the many limitations of self-administered home-based manual lymphatic drainage therapy. We began selling our more advanced Flexitouch system after receiving 510(k) clearance from the FDA in October 2006. In September 2016, we received 510(k) clearance from the FDA for the Flexitouch system in treating lymphedema of the head and neck. In June 2017, we

announced that we received 510(k) clearance from the FDA for the Flexitouch Plus, the third-generation version of our Flexitouch system. In December 2020, we received 510(k) clearance for two new indications for our Flexitouch Plus system: phlebolymphedema and lipedema. We introduced our Entre system in the United States in February 2013 and the second generation, Entre Plus, in March 2023. The Entre Plus system is sold or rented to patients who need a simple pump or who do not yet qualify for insurance reimbursement for an advanced compression device such as our Flexitouch Plus system. Nimbl, our next generation pneumatic compression platform, received 510(k) clearance in June 2024 and, beginning in October 2024, is commercially available throughout the United States for treatment of upper extremity lymphedema, and subsequently was commercially launched for lower extremity lymphedema in February 2025. Sales and rentals of our lymphedema products generated $278.4 million, or 84%, of our revenue in 2025, and $259.4 million, or 89%, of our revenue in 2024.

On September 8, 2021, we acquired the assets of the AffloVest airway clearance product line. AffloVest is a portable, battery-powered, wearable vest that provides airway clearance to treat patients with chronic respiratory conditions such as bronchiectasis or conditions resulting from neuromuscular disorders. The AffloVest product line generated $51.1 million, or 16%, of our revenue in 2025, and $33.6 million, or 11%, of our revenue in 2024.

To support the growth of our business, we continue to invest in our commercial infrastructure, consisting of our direct sales force, DME sales team, patient education team, reimbursement capabilities, and clinical expertise. We are a national, accredited provider of home medical equipment services approved for coverage by private payers, Medicare, the Veterans Administration and certain Medicaid programs in the United States. Our field commercial team is focused on increasing clinician awareness of our lymphedema solutions. As of December 31, 2025, we employed 166 account managers and 166 specialists for our lymphedema products and a team of 19 specialists supporting our airway clearance products. This compares to 169 account managers and 111 specialists for our lymphedema products and a team of 18 specialists supporting our airway clearance products as of December 31, 2024.

Our reimbursement function includes payer relations and reimbursement operations. Our payer relations function focuses on payer policy development, education, payer contract negotiations, and data analysis. Our reimbursement operations function is responsible for verifying patient insurance benefits, individual patient case development, prior authorization submissions, case follow-up, and appeals when necessary. Our clinical function, consisting of a scientific advisory board, in-house therapists and nurses, and our Chief Medical Officer, serves as a resource to clinicians and patients and guides our development of clinical evidence in support of our products. We believe these investments are critical to driving payer, clinician and patient adoption of our technologies, and together with our commercial infrastructure, represent a significant competitive advantage.

Health insurance coverage for our Flexitouch Plus, Entre Plus and Nimbl systems is in place with private payers, Medicare, the Veterans Administration and certain Medicaid programs. Based on our estimates, we are contracted or enrolled as an in-network provider with payers covering over 278 million lives in the United States. In 2025, we served over 84,000 patients with our compression therapy devices and cumulatively have served over 635,000 patients since they launched.

AffloVest also benefits from a relatively mature reimbursement landscape. Health insurance coverage is in place for High Frequency Chest Wall Oscillation ("HFCWO") vest therapy with Medicare and most private insurers. Respiratory DME partners serve the role of receiving prescriptions, verifying coverage criteria, shipping, billing and training the patient.

The lymphatic system, a fundamental part of the cardiovascular system, consists of lymph vessels and lymph organs that protect the body against harmful bacteria and transport lymph fluid from the body's tissues back to the cardiovascular system. Lymph vessels are thin-walled capillaries that absorb fluids, bacteria and

proteins, and propel them to lymph nodes, small lymph organs that filter and process the lymph fluid by eliminating waste and bacteria. Lymph nodes are located in several areas of the body, including superficial and deep lymph nodes under each arm, at the hip, in the groin, above the collar bones in the neck, in the abdomen, tonsils and spleen, and in bone marrow. Lymph vessels and lymph nodes work together with larger lymph structures to help maintain a normal healthy fluid balance.

headings: Risks Related to Our Business, Operations and Strategy
Changes to the level of Medicare coverage or coverage criteria for our products could have an adverse effect on our business and results of operations.
If we are unable to achieve and maintain adequate levels of coverage or reimbursement for our products, our business and results of operations will be adversely affected.
If we are unable to expand, manage and maintain our direct sales and marketing organizations, as well as our relationships with distributors, we may not be able to generate anticipated revenue.
We utilize third-party, single-source suppliers for some components and materials used in our products, and the loss of any of these suppliers could have an adverse impact on our business.
Our long-term growth depends on awareness and adoption of our products.
Our revenue is primarily generated from our lymphedema products and we are therefore highly dependent on these products.
Current or worsening economic conditions, including inflation, rising interest rates or a recession, could adversely affect our business and financial condition.
Our business, financial condition and results of operations may be negatively impacted by health epidemics or other outbreaks.
Consolidation in the healthcare industry could lead to demands for price concessions, which may impact our ability to sell our products at prices necessary to support our current business strategies.
Changes in government trade policies, including additional tariffs and the resulting consequences, may have a material adverse impact on our business and results of operations.
Increases in our operating costs could have an adverse effect on our financial condition and results of operations.

We compete and may compete in the future against other companies, some of which have longer operating histories, more established products or greater resources than we do, which may harm our business.
Our long-term growth depends on our ability to develop and commercialize additional products.
Failure to effectively implement technology initiatives or anticipate future technology needs or demands could adversely affect our business or financial results.
It is difficult to forecast future performance and our financial results may vary from forecasts and may fluctuate from quarter to quarter.
If physicians fail to properly document medical records for patients using our products, our business could be adversely impacted.
The size of the market for our products is an estimate, and may be smaller than we believe.
We may be unable to manage our growth effectively.
Our ability to maintain our competitive position depends on our ability to attract, integrate and retain key executives and highly qualified personnel.
Changes in reimbursement coding could impair our ability to receive reimbursement for our products.
If the quality of our products does not meet the expectations of physicians or patients, then our brand and reputation could suffer and our business could be adversely impacted.
We may be adversely affected by natural disasters and other catastrophic events, and by man-made problems such as terrorism or violence, that could disrupt our business operations.
Acquisition activity involves substantial risks, and we may not be able to successfully integrate newly acquired companies or businesses.
If we commercialize any products outside of the United States, a variety of risks associated with international operations could impact our strategy and adversely affect our future growth.
Government Regulation, Compliance and Legal Risks
paragraphs: Risk factors which could cause actual results to differ from our expectations and which could negatively impact our financial condition and results of operations are discussed below and elsewhere in this report. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that are currently not believed to be significant to our business may also affect our actual results and could harm our business, financial condition and results of operations. If any of the risks or uncertainties described below or any additional risks and uncertainties actually occur, our business, results of operations and financial condition could be materially and adversely affected.

Determinations of which products or services will be reimbursed under Medicare can be developed at the national level through a National Coverage Determination, or NCD, by CMS, or at the local level through a Local Coverage Determination, or LCD, by the two regional Durable Medical Equipment (DME) Medicare Administrative Contractors (MACs), which are private contractors that process and pay claims on behalf of CMS for different regions. The NCD for Pneumatic Compression Devices (PCDs) was established on January 14, 2002 and the LCD for PCDs was established by the MACs on October 1, 2015. On November 14, 2024 the LCD for PCDs was retired, and therefore the NCD will apply to all PCDs. We are not able to predict how the application of the NCD to PCDs that were previously covered by the LCD will impact coverage determinations, but unfavorable interpretations may occur. In addition, beginning April 13, 2026, CMS will require prior authorization requests ("PARs") for pneumatic compression devices billed under the HCPCS codes for our PCD products. While the impacts of the new PAR process are uncertain at this time, the requirement to obtain PARs related to our products could result in increased claim denials, delays in shipments due to additional administrative requirements associated with the process and other negative effects. The new PAR process could adversely affect coverage matters, particularly during the initial implementation phase of the new requirement.

The remaining NCDs may be subject to review and revision from time to time, and a new LCD may be developed, which may not be favorable for coverage of our products. Additional NCDs or LCDs, or changes in NCDs or LCDs for our products, could have adverse effects on our business. Further, we believe that a reduction or elimination of coverage or reimbursement of our products by Medicare would likely cause some commercial third-party payers to implement similar reductions in their coverage or reimbursement of our products. Given the evolving nature of the healthcare industry and ongoing healthcare cost reforms, we are and will continue to be subject to changes in the level of Medicare coverage for our products, and unfavorable coverage determinations at the national or local level could adversely affect our business and results of operations.

Any decline in the amount payers are willing to pay for our products could create pricing pressure for us. If we are forced to lower the price we charge for our products, our gross margins will decrease, which will adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations. Also, insurance benefits vary substantially by health plan, meaning that some patients have high annual out-of-pocket medical costs, which may make it difficult for those patients to afford our products.

Third-party payers, whether foreign or domestic, or governmental or commercial, are developing increasingly sophisticated methods of controlling healthcare costs. In the United States reimbursement for our products exists among the majority of third-party payers. However, reimbursement trends and coverage for our products can differ significantly between third-party payers. In addition, payers, including Medicare, continually review existing technologies for continued coverage and can, without notice, deny or reverse coverage for existing products. We believe any reduction or elimination of coverage or reimbursement of our products by Medicare would likely cause many commercial third-party payers to implement similar reductions or elimination of their coverage or reimbursement of our products. If we are unable to expand coverage of our products by additional commercial payers, or if third-party payers that currently cover or reimburse for our products reverse or limit their coverage or reimbursement in the future, our business and results of operations could be adversely affected.

Further, we believe that future coverage and reimbursement may be subject to increased restrictions, such as additional preauthorization requirements. If we are unable to satisfy any new preauthorization requirements or adjust to any future new restrictions on our products, third-party coverage and reimbursement may be limited in the future, which could have an adverse impact on our business.

In July 2022, we launched Kylee™ a free mobile app that makes it easier for patients to manage their conditions by tracking treatments and symptoms, as well as having direct access to educational resources. Flexitouch Plus and Nimbl devices include Bluetooth technology, which is viewable using Kylee.

For the year ended December 31, 2025, we generated revenue of $329.5 million and had net income of $19.1 million, compared to revenue of $293.0 million and net income of $17.0 million for the year ended December 31, 2024, and revenue of $274.4 million and net income of $28.5 million for the year ended December 31, 2023. Our primary sources of capital since our initial public offering in 2016 have been from operating income, bank financing and our public offering in February 2023.
We operate in one segment for financial reporting purposes.

General global economic downturns and macroeconomic trends, including heightened inflation, capital market volatility, interest rate fluctuations, increased unemployment and economic slowdown or recession, may result in unfavorable conditions that could negatively affect demand for our products and exacerbate some of the other risks that affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.

paragraphs: Tactile Systems Technology, Inc. ("we," "us," and "our") 為一間醫療科技公司，開發並提供創新醫療器材，用以治療未被充分照顧的慢性疾病。我們最初於1995年1月30日在明尼蘇達州註冊成立，公司名稱為Tactile Systems Technology, Inc.。於2006年，我們設立了一間合併公司，並於2006年7月21日與該合併公司合併，使我們重新註冊為德拉華州公司。合併後的公司承襲原名稱Tactile Systems Technology, Inc.，並於2013年9月開始以"Tactile Medical"為商號進行業務。

我們的使命是協助患有慢性疾病的患者，使其在家能過得更好，並能自行照顧自己。我們致力於提升在家治療未被充分照顧的慢性疾病的照護標準，以改善患者的治療結果與生活品質，並協助控制醫療支出的上升。我們的治療重點領域為(1)血管疾病，目標為提升治療淋巴水腫與慢性靜脈功能不全的照護標準；(2)腫瘤學，其中淋巴水腫是癌症存活者常見的後遺症；(3)為患有慢性呼吸道疾病的患者提供氣道清潔療法。我們擁有獨特且可擴展的平台，用以提供美國的居家醫療解決方案。這種逐步發展的居家照護模式已被政策制定者與保險給付者視為控制醫療成本上升的關鍵。我們的解決方案提供成本效益高、臨牀證實有效的長期治療方案，用以治療這些慢性疾病。

我們通常在淋巴水腫產品組閤中採用直接對患者與醫療提供者模式，透過此模式，我們從臨牀專業人員獲得患者轉介，為患者及其臨牀專業人員管理保險申報，直接將我們的解決方案送達患者，並對患者進行正確使用我們解決方案的訓練。此模式使我們能直接與患者與臨牀專業人員互動，這兩者都是我們能提供臨牀證據與教育的關鍵對象。針對我們的呼吸道療法產品，我們採用耐用醫療器材（"DME"）的分銷模式，透過此模式，我們將AffloVest產品銷售給認證的DME供應商，其代表會收集並提交給付者申報文件，訓練患者使用該設備，並提供持續的患者支援。

淋巴水腫是一種慢性水腫，會發生在手臂、腿、頸部、胸腔或其他身體部位，當淋巴管無法有效地將富含蛋白質的淋巴液從這些區域排出時就會發生。淋巴水腫是一種漸進性疾病，會隨時間惡化，目前尚無已知的治療方法。慢性靜脈功能不全是一種情況，當靜脈壁和/或靜脈瓣膜無法有效運作時，會導致血液難以從受影響區域返回心臟。靜脈淋巴水腫是淋巴水腫與慢性靜脈功能不全的結合。當靜脈系統無法有效地將血液從下肢運迴心臟時，可能會導致靜脈高血壓，並在下肢形成疼痛且難以癒合的傷口，稱為靜脈性腿部潰瘍。靜脈高血壓也可能導致肢體液體積增加，使淋巴系統過負，進而導致淋巴水腫。我們的專利Flexitouch、Entre和Nimbl系統是臨牀證實的居家解決方案，用以治療患有血管疾病如淋巴水腫的患者。患有淋巴水腫的患者通常由血管外科醫生、血管內科醫生、腫瘤照護團隊、傷口醫生、護士和治療師進行治療。

我們目前的淋巴水腫產品為Flexitouch Plus、Entre Plus和Nimbl系統。我們Flexitouch系統的前身於2002年7月獲得美國食品藥物管理局（"FDA"）的510(k)認可，並於此後推出此係統以解決自體執行的居家淋巴引流療法的許多限制。我們在2006年10月獲得FDA的510(k)認可後，開始銷售更進階的Flexitouch系統。2016年9月，我們獲得FDA的510(k)認可，用以治療頭頸部淋巴水腫。2017年6月，我們

宣佈已獲得FDA的510(k)認可，用以治療Flexitouch Plus，這是我們Flexitouch系統的第三代版本。2020年12月，我們獲得FDA的510(k)認可，用於Flexitouch Plus系統的兩項新適應症：靜脈淋巴水腫和脂質沉積症。我們於2013年2月在美國推出Entre系統，並於2023年3月推出第二代Entre Plus系統。Entre Plus系統是銷售或出租給需要簡單泵浦或尚未符合保險給付的先進壓縮裝置（如我們的Flexitouch Plus系統）的患者。Nimbl，我們下一代的氣壓壓縮平台，於2024年6月獲得510(k)認可，並自2024年10月起在美國上市，用以治療上肢淋巴水腫，隨後於2025年2月正式上市用以治療下肢淋巴水腫。我們淋巴水腫產品的銷售與出租在2025年產生了278.4 百萬美元，佔我們營業收入的84%，而在2024年則產生了259.4 百萬美元，佔我們營業收入的89%。
2021年9月8日，我們收購了AffloVest氣道清潔產品線的資產。AffloVest是一種便攜式、電池供電、可穿戴的背心，用以提供氣道清潔療法，用以治療患有慢性呼吸道疾病的患者，如支氣管擴張症或因神經肌肉疾病引起的病症。AffloVest產品線在2025年產生了51.1 百萬美元，佔我們營業收入的16%，而在2024年則產生了33.6 百萬美元，佔我們營業收入的11%。

為支持本公司業務的成長，我們持續投資於商業基礎建設，包含直接銷售團隊、DME銷售團隊、病人教育團隊、報銷能力及臨牀專業知識。本公司為美國境內被核准提供居家醫療設備服務的國家級認證機構，並獲私營保險機構、醫療保險（Medicare）、退伍軍人管理局（Veterans Administration）及部分醫療補助（Medicaid）計畫的覆蓋認可。我們的現場商業團隊專注於提高臨牀人員對我們淋巴水腫解決方案的認知。截至2025年12月31日，我們聘請了166位帳戶管理員及166位專員負責我們的淋巴水腫產品，並有一支19人專員團隊支援我們的呼吸道清潔產品。這與截至2024年12月31日的169位帳戶管理員及111位專員負責我們的淋巴水腫產品，並有一支18人專員團隊支援我們的呼吸道清潔產品相比。

我們的報銷功能包含保險機構關係及報銷作業。我們的保險機構關係功能專注於保險機構政策制定、教育、保險機構契約談判及資料分析。我們的報銷作業功能負責驗證病人保險權益、個別病人案例開發、事前授權申請、案例後續追蹤及必要時的異議處理。我們的臨牀功能包含科學顧問委員會、內部治療師及護理人員，以及我們的首席醫療官，為臨牀人員及病人提供資源，並引導我們開發支持產品的臨牀證據。我們認為這些投資對推動保險機構、臨牀人員及病人採用我們的技術至關重要，與我們的商業基礎建設共同代表顯著的競爭優勢。

我們的Flexitouch Plus、Entre Plus及Nimbl系統的醫療保險覆蓋已與私營保險機構、醫療保險（Medicare）、退伍軍人管理局（Veterans Administration）及部分醫療補助（Medicaid）計畫建立。根據我們的估計，我們已與覆蓋美國超過278百萬人口的保險機構簽約或註冊為網路內提供者。2025年，我們透過壓縮治療設備服務了超過84,000位病人，自這些產品上市以來，累計已服務超過635,000位病人。
AffloVest也受益於相對成熟的報銷環境。高頻率胸壁震盪（"HFCWO"）背心治療的醫療保險覆蓋已與醫療保險（Medicare）及大多數私營保險機構建立。呼吸道DME夥伴擔任接收處方、驗證覆蓋條件、運送、開立帳單及培訓病人的角色。
淋巴系統是心血管系統的基本組成部分，包含淋巴管及淋巴器官，用以保護身體免受有害細菌侵害，並將淋巴液從身體組織回送至心血管系統。淋巴管是薄壁的毛細血管，吸收液體、細菌及蛋白質，並將其推動至淋巴結，這些小型淋巴器官透過過濾及處理淋巴液，去除廢物及細菌。淋巴結位於身體的多個區域，包括每個手臂的皮下及深層淋巴結、髖部、腹股溝、頸部鎖骨上方、腹部、扁桃體及脾臟，以及骨髓中。
淋巴管及淋巴結與較大的淋巴結構共同作用，協助維持正常的健康體液平衡。

paragraphs: 下列對我們財務狀況及營運成果的討論與分析，應與我們的合併財務報表及其附註說明一併閱讀，並包含於本報告其他部分。
本「管理層討論與分析財務狀況及營運成果」專注於2025年與2024年之間的年對年比較。有關2023年營運成果及2024年與2023年之間的年對年比較，且未包含於本10-K年度報告中之內容，可參閱我們2024年12月31日財務年度的10-K年度報告，該報告於2025年2月18日提交至證券交易委員會（SEC）的「管理層討論與分析財務狀況及營運成果」部分，位於第二部分，第7項。

本公司為醫療科技公司，專門開發與商業化美國的醫療器材。我們的使命是協助患有慢性疾病的患者改善生活品質，並能在家中照顧自己。我們致力於提升對未被充分照顧的慢性疾病患者的照護標準，以改善患者結果與生活品質，並協助控制醫療支出的上升。我們的治療重點領域為（1）血管疾病，目標為提升治療淋巴水腫與慢性靜脈功能不全的照護標準；（2）腫瘤學，其中淋巴水腫是癌症存活者常見的後遺症；以及（3）為患有慢性呼吸道疾病的患者提供氣道清潔療法。我們擁有獨特且可擴展的平台，用以提供美國的居家醫療解決方案。這種逐步發展的居家照護模式已被政策制定者與保險給付者認可為控制醫療成本上升的關鍵。我們的解決方案提供成本效益高、臨牀證實的長期治療方案，用以治療這些慢性疾病。我們通常在淋巴水腫產品線中採用直接對患者與醫療提供者模式，透過此模式，我們從臨牀專業人員獲得患者轉介，為患者及其臨牀專業人員處理保險申報，直接將解決方案交付患者並進行正確使用訓練。此模式使我們能直接與患者與臨牀專業人員互動，這兩者都是我們可以提供臨牀證據與教育的重要對象。針對我們的呼吸道治療產品，我們採用耐用醫療器材（"DME"）的分銷模式，透過此模式，我們將AffloVest產品銷售給認證的DME供應商，其代表會收集並提交給付者申報文件，訓練患者使用該設備，並提供持續的患者支持。

我們目前的淋巴水腫產品為Flexitouch Plus、Entre Plus與Nimbl氣壓壓縮泵系統，我們的氣道清潔產品為一種高頻率胸壁震動（"HFCWO"）設備，稱為AffloVest。Flexitouch系統產品線被視為一種先進的氣壓壓縮設備。第一代Flexitouch系統於2002年7月獲得美國食品藥物管理局（"FDA"）的510(k)認可，引入一種醫療器材技術，用以解決自發性居家手動淋巴引流療法的許多限制。第二代Flexitouch系統於2006年10月獲得FDA的510(k)認可。2016年9月，我們獲得FDA的510(k)認可，用以治療頭頸部淋巴水腫。第三代Flexitouch Plus於2017年6月獲得FDA的510(k)認可。2020年12月，我們獲得FDA的510(k)認可，為Flexitouch Plus系統新增兩種適應症：靜脈淋巴水腫與脂質沉積症。Entre系統產品線與Nimbl產品線被視為基礎或簡單的氣壓壓縮設備。這些系統會銷售或出租給需要簡單泵或尚未符合保險給付條件的患者，例如Flexitouch Plus系統。我們於2013年2月在美國推出Entre系統，該設備由Thermotek, Inc.製造，並於2010年獲得FDA認可。2015年，我們獲得我們第一代Entre系統的FDA認可，第二代Entre Plus於2023年3月推出。Nimbl，我們新一代的氣壓壓縮平台，於2024年6月獲得FDA的510(k)認可，並於2024年10月開始商業化銷售上肢淋巴水腫，於2025年2月開始商業化銷售下肢淋巴水腫。Nimbl已取代我們大部分Entre系統的訂單，我們
預期會持續如此。我們淋巴水腫產品的銷售與出租，分別在2025年12月31日與2024年12月31日財務年度中，佔我們營業收入的84%與89%。
2021年9月8日，我們取得AffloVest氣道清潔產品線的資產。AffloVest是一種便攜式、可穿戴的背心，用以提供氣道清潔療法，用以治療患有慢性呼吸道疾病的患者，例如支氣管擴張症或因神經肌肉疾病所導致的病症。在2025年12月31日與2024年12月31日財務年度中，AffloVest的銷售分別佔我們營業收入的16%與11%。

為支持我們業務的成長，我們持續投資於我們的商業基礎設施，包括獨立的淋巴水腫與呼吸道銷售團隊、行銷團隊（包括臨牀教育計畫）、患者教育團隊、給付能力（reimbursement）功能與臨牀專業知識。我們透過直接對患者與臨牀專業人員的模式來行銷我們的淋巴水腫產品。AffloVest設備透過美國各地的呼吸道耐用醫療器材供應商銷售，這些供應商為患者提供服務並向第三方給付者申報產品費用。我們聘請了一小羣呼吸道專科醫生，用以教育DME代表、為目標臨牀專業人員進行產品展示，並支援與AffloVest相關的技術問題。截至2025年12月31日，我們聘請了166位帳戶管理員與166位專科醫生來支援我們的淋巴水腫產品，並有19位專科醫生支援我們的氣道清潔產品。這與截至2024年12月31日的169位帳戶管理員與111位專科醫生支援我們的淋巴水腫產品，以及18位專科醫生支援我們的氣道清潔產品相比。
我們投資於給付能力功能，以提升作業效率並增強個別給付者的專業知識，同時持續我們的戰略重點，即給付者發展。我們的給付者關係功能專注於給付者政策發展、教育、契約談判與數據分析。我們的給付能力作業功能負責驗證患者的保險福利、個別患者案例開發、預先授權申請、案例追蹤，以及必要時的爭議處理。
我們也設有臨牀團隊，包含科學顧問委員會、內部治療師與護理人員，以及首席醫療官，作為臨牀人員與患者的資源，並引導臨牀證據的發展，以支持我們的產品。大多數臨牀研究需要觀察與臨牀人員與患者的互動，以監測結果與進展。
我們依賴第三方製造商進行零組件的採購、控制器的組裝以及與我們系統搭配使用的衣物製造。我們進行與產品搭配使用的衣物最終組裝，執行品質保證，並從位於明尼蘇達州的廠區發貨。我們也於明尼蘇達州廠區製造與發貨 AffloVest 裝置。
2022 年 7 月，我們推出了 Kylee™ 這款免費行動應用程式，讓患者更容易管理其病情，透過追蹤治療與症狀，並可直接存取教育資源。Flexitouch Plus 與 Nimbl 裝置包含藍牙技術，可透過 Kylee 進行查看。

截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日財年，我們產生營業收入 329.5 百萬美元，淨收入為 19.1 百萬美元，與 2024 年 12 月 31 日財年產生營業收入 293.0 百萬美元、淨收入 17.0 百萬美元，以及 2023 年 12 月 31 日財年產生營業收入 274.4 百萬美元、淨收入 28.5 百萬美元相比。自我們 2016 年首次公開發行股票以來，我們的主要資金來源為營運收入、銀行融資以及 2023 年 2 月的公開發行。
我們在財務報導目的上僅運作一個應報告分部。
全球總體經濟衰退與總體經濟趨勢，包括通貨膨脹升高、資本市場波動、利率波動、失業率增加以及經濟減速或衰退，可能會導致不利的環境，可能影響我們產品的需求，並加劇影響我們業務、財務狀況與營運成果的一些其他風險。

headings: 與我們業務、營運及策略相關之風險
Medicare 覆蓋範圍或覆蓋標準之變更，可能對我們之業務及營運結果產生不利影響。
若我們無法達成並維持足夠之覆蓋範圍或報銷水平，將對我們之業務及營運結果產生不利影響。
若我們無法擴展、管理及維持我們之直接銷售與行銷組織，以及與經銷商之關係，我們可能無法達成預期之營收。
我們針對部分零組件及材料使用第三方單一來源供應商，若失去任何這些供應商，將對我們之業務產生不利影響。
我們之長期成長取決於產品之認知度與採用率。
我們之營收主要來自淋巴水腫產品，因此我們高度依賴這些產品。
目前或惡化之經濟情況，包括通貨膨脹、利率上升或經濟衰退，可能對我們之業務及財務狀況產生不利影響。
本公司之業務、財務狀況及營運成果可能因健康疫情或其他疫情而受到負面影響。
醫療保健產業之整併可能導致對價格讓步之需求，此可能影響本公司銷售產品之能力，使其無法以支撐現有業務策略之價格進行銷售。
政府貿易政策之變動，包括額外關稅及相關後果，可能對本公司之業務及營運成果產生重大不利影響。
本公司營運成本之增加可能對財務狀況及營運成果產生負面影響。
本公司與其他公司競爭，未來亦可能與其他公司競爭，部分公司具有較長之營運歷史、更成熟之產品或更多資源，此可能對本公司業務造成損害。
本公司之長期成長取決於本公司開發及商業化更多產品之能力。
未能有效實施科技計畫或預見未來科技需求或需求，可能對本公司業務或財務成果產生負面影響。
預測未來表現困難，本公司財務成果可能與預測不同，且可能於各季度間波動。
若醫師未能正確為使用我們產品的病患記錄醫療紀錄，將可能對本公司業務造成不利影響。
我們產品的市場規模為估計值，可能小於我們所認為的規模。
我們可能無法有效管理成長。
本公司維持競爭地位的能力，取決於吸引、整合及留住關鍵高階主管與具備高素質人才的能力。
賠償編碼的變更可能影響本公司獲得產品賠償的能力。
若我們的產品品質未符合醫師或病患的期待，將可能影響本公司品牌與聲譽，並對業務造成不利影響。
本公司可能因天然災害及其他重大事故，以及人為問題如恐怖攻擊或暴力事件而受到不利影響，這些事件可能幹擾本公司業務運作。
併購活動涉及重大風險，本公司可能無法成功整合新併購的公司或業務。
若我們在美國境外商業化任何產品，與國際營運相關的各種風險可能影響我們的策略，並對我們未來的成長產生不利影響。

{'text': '有關哪些產品或服務可獲得醫療保險（Medicare）補償的決定，可透過美國醫療保險局（CMS）於國家層面透過國家覆蓋決定（National Coverage Determination, NCD）制定，或透過兩大區域性醫療設備（Durable Medical Equipment, DME）醫療保險行政承包商（Medicare Administrative Contractors, MACs）於地方層面透過地方覆蓋決定（Local Coverage Determination, LCD）制定，這些MACs為私人承包商，代表CMS處理並支付不同區域的申報。Pneumatic Compression Devices（PCDs）的NCD於2002年1月14日建立，而PCDs的LCD則於2015年10月1日由MACs建立。2024年11月14日，PCDs的LCD被廢止，因此NCD將適用於所有PCDs。我們無法預測NCD適用於原先由LCD覆蓋的PCDs將如何影響覆蓋決定，但不利的解釋可能發生。此外，自2026年4月13日起，CMS將要求對我們PCD產品以HCPCS代碼申報的產品進行事前授權請求（Prior Authorization Requests, PARs）。雖然目前新PAR程序的影響尚不確定，但取得與我們產品相關的PARs的必要性，可能會導致更多申報被拒絕、因程序附加行政要求而延遲出貨，以及其他負面影響。新PAR程序可能在新要求的初始實施階段對覆蓋事項產生不利影響。'}

{'text': '剩餘的NCD可能隨時受到審查與修訂，並可能開發出新的LCD，而新LCD可能對我們產品的覆蓋不具利於。新增的NCD或LCD，或對我們產品的NCD或LCD變更，可能對我們業務產生不利影響。此外，我們認為，若我們產品的覆蓋或補償被醫療保險（Medicare）減少或取消，將可能導致許多商業第三方支付者對我們產品的覆蓋或補償實施類似的減少。考慮到醫療產業的持續演變及醫療成本改革的進行，我們將持續面臨醫療保險對我們產品覆蓋程度的變動，且國家或地方層面的不利覆蓋決定可能對我們業務及營業成果產生不利影響。'}
{'text': '若支付者願意為我們產品支付的金額減少，將可能對我們造成價格壓力。若我們被迫降低產品售價，將導致我們毛利率下降，進而對我們業務、財務狀況及營業成果產生不利影響。此外，保險福利因健康計畫而異，意味著某些患者每年的醫療自付費用較高，這可能使這些患者難以負擔我們的產品。'}

{'text': '無論為國內或國際、政府或商業機構的第三方支付者，皆正在發展越來越複雜的方法來控制醫療成本。在美國，我們產品的補償已於大多數第三方支付者中存在。然而，我們產品的補償趨勢與覆蓋情況在不同第三方支付者之間可能有顯著差異。此外，支付者，包括醫療保險（Medicare），持續審查現有技術以維持覆蓋，並可能在未事先通知的情況下拒絕或撤回現有產品的覆蓋。我們認為，若醫療保險（Medicare）對我們產品的覆蓋或補償減少或取消，將可能導致許多商業第三方支付者對我們產品的覆蓋或補償實施類似的減少或取消。若我們無法透過更多商業支付者擴大我們產品的覆蓋或補償，或若目前覆蓋或補償我們產品的第三方支付者未來撤回或限制其覆蓋或補償，將可能對我們業務及營業成果產生不利影響。'}
{'text': '此外，我們認為未來的覆蓋與補償可能受到更多限制，例如額外的事前授權要求。若我們無法符合任何新的事前授權要求，或無法適應未來對我們產品的任何新限制，第三方的覆蓋與補償可能在未來受到限制，這可能對我們業務產生不利影響。'}
